label: Reflationary Late-Cycle Overheat
blurb: Growth is re-accelerating (GDPNow 4.4% for Q3 after a soft 1.5% Q2; payrolls +162K) while an energy shock pushes headline inflation back up (CPI 3.4% flat, PPI 5.4% ↑, fuel +27% y/y). That is Quadrant 2 — rising growth AND rising prices — and Quadrant 2 is where central banks tighten. Core CPI at 2.4% is the one serious argument that this is supply rather than demand.
path6m: Up and to the right, out of the ①/④ border: growth re-accelerated from a 1.5% Q2 to a 4.4% nowcast while an energy shock pushed inflation back up. Deep into ② now.
punishes: Long-duration bonds · high-multiple tech · the domestic consumer
nextCatalyst: Sep 16 FOMC and retail sales (both axes) · Oct 2 payrolls (growth axis)
